sampling.measures: Exported frames against the browser's buildVideoSamplingPlan for the notional source clip: frame count, analysis size, timestamps.

features.measures: The authoritative whole-pixel matcher with the browser's options on every adjacent pair, against the true correspondence of each source feature (exact depth reprojected into the target, occlusion-aware). A match is correct within 1.5 px; counts, precision and median error are gated on the worst pair. It scores the first-pass baseline matcher; matches the reconstruction substitutes (motion-guided or recovery passes) are not exposed by the core and are not scored here.

seed.measures: The chosen calibrated seed pair against the true relative pose: rotation error and translation-direction error; the true baseline, true triangulation angle and the rotation-only residual are reported per candidate.

registration.measures: Registered views; camera-center RMSE divided by the true trajectory span and the worst camera orientation error, both through one pose alignment (orientation-derived rotation, center-fitted scale and translation).

dense.measures: Each reference's dense depth against the true depth through the same grid pixel, after removing that reference's scale bias (the registration owns scale; the bias is reported). Accurate coverage is the share of sampled grid pixels with a point within 2 % of the true depth. The scale bias itself is bounded: a reference whose depths disagree with the camera alignment by more than 10 % fails.

mesh.measures: The mesh through each reference's local alignment against the true heightfield: median centroid error, share of triangles more than 5 cm off the surface (unsupported), coverage of the 5 cm surface cells two registered cameras see unoccluded, cells covered by more than one reference (duplicated overlap), and topology: cross-reference triangles, shared vertices, and the components of the graph of meshed reference patches joined by cross-reference triangles (1 when every patch connects).

texture.measures: The reference-view material bake: textured triangle share, and for four barycentric samples per textured triangle the distance between the texel's source pixel and the true projection of its surface point, and its color against the true shaded albedo at that point (8-bit levels).

fixtures.intent: Small lateral steps (0.15 m per sampling interval) along a Trevi-like façade 6 m away with 0.45 m relief. Relief parallax is 0.63 px per interval, below the 1.25 px rotation-only gate, and 10.7 px over the clip. Cameras should register.

expected_failures.reason: No adjacent pair passes the residual-parallax gate (0.0–0.38 px against 0.55 px), so no seed pair is accepted.
No camera registers without a seed pair.

fixtures.intent: The same façade and viewing direction with the camera rotating in place by the pan's image motion. Negative control: the translation-baseline gate must reject it and no camera may register.

A pan (0.2 m per interval) over a façade 4 m away with 1 m relief on gentle slopes; adjacent views overlap by more than 90 %, so neighbouring reference patches see the same surface. The truth is one connected surface, so overlapping patches must share topology.

baseline.notes: Every stage passes. Overlap ownership is decided in the higher-priority reference camera's image, only between original mesh components joined (transitively) by fusion-accepted seam pairs, with a 3.5 % relative depth bound after removing the patch pair's depth scale (anchored at the fusion-accepted seam vertices between that patch pair); where an owner camera judged a triangle, the looser 3D test does not overrule it. Duplicated coverage 0.095 (max 0.1), unsupported share 0.098, surface coverage 0.390, 135 cross-reference triangles (seam pairs across evidence origins link patches but keep separate vertices), one patch-graph component. Seam triangles at least 80 % owned are trimmed (0.6 % of the accepted mesh area on the triangles' planes, reported in the merge diagnostic); the trimmed seams are not re-stitched (#137), so the reported mesh has more connected components (141) than before the trim (40).
